riley (eng-sre): INC: p99 decode latency spike observed across prod-us-east-1 pools, alerted at 09:12 UTC :rotating_light:
inc-bot: INCIDENT OPENED: decode-latency-2078901234 severity=high impacted_services=[hosted-api,dedicated-inference]
ops-bot: metric alert: hosted-api.decode.latency.p99 = 1.8s (baseline 0.45s), streaming stall rate increased x6, 5xx rate +2.3%
kevin (oncall): I'm awake, taking first touch. Maria, can you confirm if any kernel/rt rollouts happened in the last 2 hours?
maria (runtime): yes we pushed a TRT + flash-attn kernel bundle to canary pools at 07:40 UTC to test new fused matmul path. Canary looked fine. No full rollout yet but a config flip to compiler flags landed at 08:50 that propagates to prod-auto-rollout groups.
jasmin (eng-runtime): seeing increased page faults and decode stalls in the host logs. stack traces point at trt_kernel_launch -> flash_attn_forward in many failing requests. sample log:
```
[2026-03-14T09:10:21Z] request_id=abc123 decode_ms=780 p99
E: cudnn/kernel_launch: block=... err=CUDASUCCESS
W: paging: kernel fallback triggered, fallback_path=compile_and_run
trace: flash_attn_forward: nvrtc_compile() took 320ms
```
kevin (oncall): customer impact? any inbound support tickets?
sam (customer-ops): a few customers reported streaming stalls and abrupt connection closes, one enterprise saw 15% request degradation on a critical route. We opened ticket TKT-3217.
riley (eng-sre): p95 up from 120ms to 430ms, p99 from 420ms to 1.8s across the board. Tail latency correlates with sequence length > 1024 in our traces.
maria (runtime): hypothesis: the new TRTexec kernel generates longer JIT compile paths under some memory layouts causing synchronous nvrtc compiles and host-side paging under load. The compiler flag `--enable-fused-flashattn` may trigger that path.
jasmin (eng-runtime): I can reproduce locally by replaying a few long-chat traces against the canary image with the flag on. Repro steps in case useful:
```
# repro (local)
REPRO=true ./run_inference.sh --model llama-3-70b --seq-len 2048 --enable-fused-flashattn
watch -n 0.5 "tail -n 200 runtime.log | grep nvrtc | tail -n 50"
```
kevin (oncall): mitigation options? can we quickly isolate and rollback the flag propagation?
maria (runtime): immediate mitigation plan:
1) flip config `disable_auto_kernel_rollout=true` for prod-auto-rollout (prevents any further auto-propagation)
2) roll back compiler flag on active nodes: set env `REDWOOD_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1` via runtime config, restart worker pods in a staggered manner (canary -> region -> global)
3) enable warm JIT caching to avoid nvrtc compiles: set `JIT_CACHE_MODE=warm` (short-term)
4) scale dedicated-pool by +20% for the next 30m to absorb tail spikes
I'll start 1 and 2 now.
riley (eng-sre): also add fallback policy route: divert traffic for heavy-seq requests to fallback model variant `llama-3-70b-compat` (non-fused) until rollback completes. Patch to router done: `route/seq>1024 -> variant=compat`
ops-bot: rollout change accepted: config `disable_auto_kernel_rollout=true` applied to prod-auto-rollout at 09:19 UTC
maria (runtime): applying env flip on a small subset of workers in us-east-1 now. Doing rolling restarts with maxUnavailable=1 to avoid mass disruption.
jasmin (eng-runtime): after restarting 8 workers with REDWOOD_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1 we see p99 for those nodes drop to ~420ms. Confirming overall cluster improvement trend in metrics.
kevin (oncall): good. Keep restarts staggered, prioritize nodes with highest decode load. Notify support and CS about mitigation steps.
sam (customer-ops): already pinged the top 5 affected customers, letting them know we're rolling back the kernel flag and routing heavy loads to compat variant. Monitoring for errors.
riley (eng-sre): I'm enabling an emergency alert rule to watch for p99 > 1.2s and streaming stall rate > 3x baseline. Also enabling extended logs for nvrtc compile events (retention 1h).
inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in progress. rollback flag applied to subset; routing fallback active. Next update in 20m or on status change.
kevin (oncall): timeline estimate? maria?
maria (runtime): if rollbacks continue smoothly, expect traffic to fall back to normal SLOs within ~18-25 minutes (mostly JIT cache warmup and worker restarts). If we see regressions continue after full rollback, next step is full kernel bundle rollback (replacing TRT build) which takes ~45-60m.
jasmin (eng-runtime): small note: some long-running streams may still stall until client reconnect/resume because we can't retroactively change kernel mid-stream. We'll surface that in the customer comms.
kevin (oncall): thanks. I'll update the incident channel and start oncall handoff notes for the next shift. Anyone want to own postmortem?
riley (eng-sre): I'll lead the postmortem with jasmin and maria. Assigning action items:
- jasmin: gather the nvrtc traces + sample requests that triggered compiles (due EOD)
- maria: produce a timeline of config propagation and canary metrics (due tomorrow 10:00 UTC)
- kevin: compile customer impact summary and list of affected routes (due EOD)
- ops-bot: keep a copy of the applied rollback config (auto-generated)
ops-bot: rollback_config_snapshot: {"flag":"REDWOOD_DISABLE_FLASHATTN","applied_by":"maria","applied_at":"2026-03-14T09:20:12Z"}
riley (eng-sre): after-action temporary measures: block auto-rollout for 48h, add a gating test in canary that runs a small heavy-seq replay before flag flips, and add a runtime safety valve to detect nvrtc_compile > 50ms and route to compat variant automatically.
sam (customer-ops): customers updated, some reported immediate improvement after routing change. We'll keep monitoring and escalate if any reopen.
inc-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: decode-latency-2078901234 closed at 09:41 UTC. Root cause: compiler flag + TRTexec JIT path created synchronous nvrtc compiles under specific memory layouts causing host-side paging and tail spikes.
riley (eng-sre): good job team. Postmortem p0 created: PM-4512. We'll schedule a 30min blameless review tomorrow.
kevin (oncall): logging handoff: I've documented current state and mitigations in the oncall log. Next oncall please watch for residual p99 noise and re-open incident if thresholds breach.
maria (runtime): follow-ups: longer-term plan to harden JIT cache, add precompile step in deployment pipeline, and make FlashAttention rollout gated behind replay tests.
jasmin (eng-runtime): I'll create an integration test that simulates seq>1024 workload and asserts nvrtc compile count < 1 per minute under steady state.
riley (eng-sre): closing thread. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
